methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $2.3B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 7 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.0B.

private.name: Fairmat
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series E)

data.narrative:
Divergent, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company, raised $600M+ and carries a last post-money valuation of $2.3B. The valuation assessment relies on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies (1 public, 8 private) spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical for Series E advancement, implies $3.2B. Peer-median benchmarking across 7 same-sector, similar-tier comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The latter approach reflects current market pricing for robotics companies at adjacent stages and scales.

Synthesizing these methods produces a triangulated range of $1.4B (low) to $3.7B (high), with a median of $2.4B. The current $2.3B valuation sits near the center of this distribution, supported most directly by stage-progression mechanics. Key uncertainties include stage-specific capital availability and whether peer comps adequately capture Divergent's operational differentiation or market traction relative to the comparison set. The wide spread between methods ($1.6B peer-median vs. $3.2B stage-progression) reflects inherent divergence between market comparables and forward-stage expectations.
